newsitem.title: LEBANON: Flemings bullish on Solidere GDR.
newsitem.headline: Flemings bullish on Solidere GDR.

text.p: A research by Robert Fleming Securities said GDRs issued by Lebanon's biggest company Solidere, which jumped on the London Stock Exchange last week to over $17 from $12, could rise above $25.

"Heavy buying by emerging markets investors caused the GDR to rocket by 50 percent in three days," a research published by Robert Fleming Securities said. "The latest price is still a substantial discount to our estimated NAV (Net Asset Value) of $25 a GDR."

Flemings said the $25 NAV it set when Solidere issued the GDRs last November had been confirmed as a conservative valuation, since investors who had recently seen Solidere's progress in rebuilding central Beirut had pushed the GDRs closer to $25.

"We believe this trend will continue and may lead to our target being exceeded. The relative scarcity of the GDR and increasing focus by international investors should continue to put upwards pressure on the GDR," the research said. It cited the following reasons for investor interest in the GDRs:

- Progress in work on the Beirut Central District: The road network was taking shape, construction of a landmark headquarters for U.N. agencies was well advanced and restoration of preserved buildings was also advanced.
- The French retail group Printemps and the Four Seasons hotel group were negotiating for locations. Several major construction contracts were close to agreement.

- An Extraordinary General Meeting of Solidere shareholders on May 27 would propose cancelling at least $100 million of treasury stock returned to the company by owners who decided to restore their property in the Beirut Central District rather than take the shares in exchange for their rights. "It was feared that re-issuance of these shares would dilute earnings," Flemings said.
- The research said Solidere's management was "exemplary" and land prices in the Beirut Central District should appreciate rapidly as many top international clients were negotiating for locations.
